item.title: Silver Ford van (EU66WVJ) MOT expired - abandoned for 1+ year, 29th August
item.description:
This vehicle is parked at this spot since June 2025. It has been more than 1 year. This vehicle (EU66 WVJ - a Ford silver van) has not moved. MOT has also expired in March 2026 already. It doesn’t belong to any of the immediate houses around this permanently parked van. You can observe from the state of vehicle (rear tire is out of air, cobwebs on it, ruffled leaves on floor) which clearly indicates the vehicle has not moved for a long time. It is causing the nearby house owners problem as there is no space available for their guests / visitor to park their car for few hours, specially for the corner houses. Pls get this van removed given its not public road worthy as MOT expired long back and its owner/ caretaker is unknown in the neighbourhood.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Normanhurst Avenue, West Heath, Greater London

item.title: Urgent: Repeated Anti-Social Behaviour and Fire Incident at 34 Redbourne Avenue, 28th August
item.description:
I am writing to report a serious and escalating pattern of anti-social behaviour outside 34 Redbourne Avenue. This has now happened on three separate nights, and the police have been contacted on each occasion. 25 August: Someone was shouting in the street outside the property. 26 August: Someone was shouting outside 32 Redbourne Avenue and kicking rubbish bins. 28 August: The situation became much more serious. A fire was started behind a car outside 34 Redbourne Avenue. The fire service was called, and the incident was also reported to the police. These incidents do not appear to be random pranks or harmless nuisance behaviour. They seem deliberate and planned, and the situation is becoming increasingly concerning—particularly as my daughter is nearly two years old. We are very worried about the safety of residents, vehicles and nearby properties. Please could the Council investigate this urgently and advise what action can be taken, including any available CCTV review, community-safety support, environmental enforcement, or liaison with the police. Thank you for your urgent attention to this serious matter.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Redbourne Avenue, Church End, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.description:

There is also cement/concrete left on the road surface, making it uneven and hazardous for pedestrians and cyclists. The right-turn section is particularly concerning and needs attention to improve safety for all road users.

item.title: The signpost is rusty, 28th August
item.description:

There is a risk that the post could break or fall, potentially causing injury to pedestrians or damage to nearby vehicles. Please arrange for the post to be inspected and repaired or replaced as soon as possible.
